questions.question: As of March 14, 2024, which of the following is the world’s tallest statue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Statue of Unity, Gujarat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Statue of Unity, located in Gujarat, India, is the world's tallest statue, standing at a height of 182 meters (597 feet).
 
• It was unveiled on October 31, 2018, in honor of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India.
 
• The statue is situated on the banks of the Narmada River near the Sardar Sarovar Dam in Kevadia.
 
• Designed by Indian sculptor Ram V. Sutar, the statue is made of bronze-clad reinforced concrete.
 
• The project was completed at a cost of approximately ₹2,989 crore and aims to promote tourism and educate visitors about Sardar Patel's contributions to India's unity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Tall Statues in India:**

 
 
• Tathagata Tsal in Sikkim: A statue of Lord Buddha standing at 41 meters.
 
• Thiruvalluvar Statue in Kanyakumari: Dedicated to Tamil poet Thiruvalluvar, standing at 40.6 meters.
 
• Adiyogi Shiva Statue in Coimbatore: A 34-meter tall statue of Lord Shiva promoting yoga and spirituality.
 
 
 
• **Global Tall Statues:** The Spring Temple Buddha in China was previously the tallest statue in the world at 128 meters before being surpassed by the Statue of Unity.
 
• **Engineering Marvel:** The Statue of Unity is designed to withstand wind speeds of up to 180 km/h and earthquakes measuring up to 6.5 on the Richter scale.
 
• **Tourism Impact:** The Statue of Unity has become a major tourist attraction, drawing millions of visitors annually and boosting the local economy.
 
• **Cultural Significance:** Sardar Patel is remembered as the "Iron Man of India" for his role in unifying the country post-independence, making the statue a symbol of national integration.

questions.question: What was a major focus of the 61st Constitutional Amendment?

options.text: Reduction of voting age from 21 to 18 years
Reservation of seats for women in Panchayats
Abolition of Privy Purses for former rulers

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reduction of voting age from 21 to 18 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act of 1988 reduced the minimum voting age in India from 21 years to 18 years.
 
• This amendment applied to both the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assembly elections.
 
• The purpose of the amendment was to increase the participation of younger citizens in the democratic process of the country.
 
• By enabling individuals aged 18 and above to vote, the amendment aimed to provide representation to a larger section of the population, especially the youth.
 
• The 61st Amendment reflects India's commitment to empowering its youth as active participants in decision-making and governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Amendments:**

 
 
• Constitutional amendments are changes made to the Indian Constitution to address evolving societal, political, and legal needs.
 
• They are introduced as bills in Parliament and require a special majority for approval.
 
 
 
• **Voting in India:**
 
 
• Voting is a fundamental aspect of a democracy, allowing citizens to choose their representatives.
 
• In India, voting is governed by the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
 
 
 
• **Other Important Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• 42nd Amendment (1976): Known as the "Mini Constitution," it brought major changes like adding the words "Socialist" and "Secular" to the Preamble.
 
• 73rd Amendment (1992): Introduced the Panchayati Raj system to strengthen local governance.
 
 
 
• **Demographics of Youth in India:**
 
 
• India has one of the largest youth populations globally, making their participation in elections critical to shaping the nation’s future.
 
• The reduced voting age allowed approximately 35 million new voters to participate in the democratic process during its initial implementation.

questions.question: The term 'Sangam' refers to which of the following?

options.text: A literary assembly of Tamil scholars

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A literary assembly of Tamil scholars**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term 'Sangam' refers to an **assembly of Tamil scholars and poets** who gathered to create and refine Tamil literature during ancient times.
 
• This tradition is believed to have taken place in **three historical periods**, referred to as the First, Second, and Third Sangams.
 
• The Sangam literature primarily consists of **poetry and prose** that dealt with themes like love (Akam), heroism (Puram), ethics, and morals.
 
• The Sangam period (approximately 300 BCE to 300 CE) is a significant part of Tamil history and culture, marking the **golden age of Tamil literature**.
 
• Texts like **Tolkappiyam**, **Akananuru**, and **Purananuru** are prominent works of Sangam literature and provide insights into the socio-political and economic conditions of that era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangam Literature**: It is one of the oldest known collections of Tamil literary works and provides detailed information about ancient Tamil society, culture, and values.
 
• **First Sangam**: Held in the now-submerged city of Madurai, it is considered mythical, with no surviving works.
 
• **Second Sangam**: Believed to have been held in Kapadapuram, only fragments of its literature survive.
 
• **Third Sangam**: Conducted in the city of Madurai, it produced many of the Tamil literary works that survive to this day.
 
• **Impact on Modern Tamil**: The rich linguistic and literary traditions of Sangam literature have significantly influenced the development of modern Tamil language and culture.

questions.question: Which international organisation supports globalisation and free trade?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**WTO**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **World Trade Organization (WTO)** is an international body that regulates and promotes global trade between nations.
 
• It was established on **1 January 1995**, replacing the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT).
 
• The WTO aims to ensure **free, fair, and predictable trade** by eliminating barriers like tariffs, quotas, and subsidies.
 
• It provides a platform for negotiating trade agreements, resolving trade disputes, and monitoring trade policies of member countries.
 
• As of 2023, the WTO has **164 member countries**, representing over 98% of global trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Globalization:** It refers to the process by which businesses and organizations develop international influence or operate on a global scale, often facilitated by free trade and investment.
 
• **Free Trade:** A policy where goods and services move across borders without government-imposed restrictions like tariffs, quotas, or subsidies.
 
• **Trade Dispute Resolution:** The WTO provides a mechanism for resolving trade conflicts between countries, ensuring that trade flows smoothly.
 
• **Most-Favored-Nation Principle:** A foundational WTO rule that ensures all members receive equal trade advantages, preventing discrimination.
 
• **Trade Agreements:** WTO facilitates negotiations on multilateral trade agreements to reduce trade barriers and enhance economic cooperation globally.

questions.question: The desktop background is also known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wallpaper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The desktop background is commonly referred to as **Wallpaper**, which is an image or pattern displayed on the computer screen behind icons and open windows.
 
• Wallpapers can be customized according to user preferences and are supported by most operating systems, including **Windows, macOS, and Linux.**
 
• The term “wallpaper” originates from the idea of decorating a virtual space similar to physical wallpaper used in homes.
 
• Wallpapers can be static images or dynamic (moving) wallpapers, depending on the system capabilities and software used.
 
• Users can select wallpapers from the system's default options or upload their own images to personalize the desktop environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Icon:** Icons are small graphical representations of programs, files, or functions on a computer desktop, used to facilitate easy access.
 
• **Menu:** Menus are graphical elements or lists that provide access to various commands or options within a software or operating system.
 
• **File:** Files are digital containers that store data, such as text documents, images, videos, or software applications.
 
• **Dynamic Wallpapers:** These are animated or interactive wallpapers that change over time or react to user interactions.
 
• **Desktop Environment:** The desktop environment is the graphical interface through which users interact with their operating system, including elements like wallpapers, icons, menus, and taskbars.

questions.question: What can happen if rocks are not weathered in the context of the movement of Earth's materials?

options.text: Mass movement would be more frequent

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Erosion would be insignificant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Weathering is the breakdown of rocks into smaller particles, which contributes to erosion processes. Without weathering, erosion would be **insignificant** as there would be fewer loose materials to transport.
 
• Rocks that are not weathered remain intact, reducing the availability of sediments that can be moved by agents of erosion such as water, wind, and ice.
 
• Weathering creates soil and sediment, which are critical for erosion processes to occur. A lack of weathering would disrupt the dynamic movement of Earth's materials.
 
• Erosion depends on the presence of weathered particles for transport. Without weathering, landscapes would remain largely static, and Earth's surface would lack significant changes over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Weathering:** The process of breaking down rocks physically (mechanical weathering) or chemically (chemical weathering), which is essential for soil formation and sediment production.
 
• **Erosion:** The process of transporting weathered materials (soil, rock, and sediment) by natural agents such as water, wind, ice, or gravity.
 
• **Mass Movement:** The downward movement of rock and soil due to gravity. Weathered material is often a precursor to mass movements like landslides.
 
• **Soil Formation:** Weathering contributes to the creation of fertile soil, providing essential minerals and organic matter for plant growth.
 
• **Earth's Material Cycle:** Weathering and erosion are interconnected processes that drive the continuous cycle of material movement and landscape evolution on Earth's surface.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts aims to prevent money laundering in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002, was enacted by the Government of India to **combat money laundering activities**.
 
• It came into force on **1st July 2005** and aims to prevent and control money laundering while confiscating and seizing property involved in such activities.
 
• The Act empowers authorities such as the **Enforcement Directorate (ED)** to investigate and prosecute cases related to money laundering.
 
• PMLA mandates that reporting entities such as banks, financial institutions, and intermediaries maintain records of transactions and verify the identity of clients.
 
• The Act also ensures compliance with international standards set by the **Financial Action Task Force (FATF)**, a global watchdog for combating money laundering and terrorist financing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Money Laundering:**

 
 
• Money laundering refers to the process of disguising illicit funds to make them appear legitimate.
 
• It typically involves three stages: **placement, layering, and integration**.
 
• Placement refers to introducing illegal money into the financial system, layering involves obscuring the origin of funds, and integration completes the laundering process by embedding the funds into the legitimate economy.
 
 
 
• **Enforcement Directorate (ED):**
 
 
• The ED is the key agency under PMLA responsible for investigating and prosecuting money laundering cases.
 
• It has the authority to attach, confiscate properties, and take legal action against offenders.
 
 
 
• **FATF:**
 
 
• The Financial Action Task Force is an intergovernmental organization established in 1989 to combat money laundering, terrorism financing, and other related threats.
 
• India is a member of FATF and complies with its recommendations to enhance global efforts against financial crimes.
 
 
 
• **Associated Legislations:**
 
 
• **FEMA:** Foreign Exchange Management Act regulates foreign exchange transactions but does not address money laundering.
 
• **SEBI:** Securities and Exchange Board of India oversees capital markets but is not directly related to money laundering prevention.
 
• **FCRA:** Foreign Contribution Regulation Act regulates foreign contributions but does not cover money laundering.

questions.question: Which sweetener, first used in 1879, has received FDA approval for use in fruit juice beverages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saccharin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Saccharin** was discovered in 1879 by chemists Constantin Fahlberg and Ira Remsen.
 
• It is one of the oldest artificial sweeteners and has been widely used in food and beverages.
 
• The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved saccharin for use in fruit juice beverages and other food products.
 
• Saccharin is calorie-free and approximately **200–700 times sweeter than sugar**, making it a popular choice for low-calorie diets.
 
• It is commonly used in diet sodas, chewing gums, and other sugar-free products as a sweetening agent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Artificial Sweeteners:** These are chemical or natural compounds used to sweeten food and beverages without the calories of sugar.
 
• **FDA Approval Process:** The FDA evaluates artificial sweeteners for safety through rigorous testing before approving their use in food products.
 
• **Other Popular Artificial Sweeteners:** Aspartame, sucralose, and neotame are other FDA-approved sweeteners used in various foods and drinks.
 
• **Health Concerns:** While saccharin was once linked to cancer risk, subsequent studies and regulatory reviews concluded that it is safe for consumption.
 
• **Calorie-Free Benefits:** Artificial sweeteners like saccharin are helpful for individuals managing diabetes or following low-calorie diets.

questions.question: Which event marked the pivot moment in the extremist and moderate struggle during the Indian freedom struggle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surat Split**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Surat Split occurred in **1907** during the Indian National Congress session held in Surat.
 
• It marked a significant division between the **Moderates** and **Extremists** within the Indian National Congress.
 
• The Moderates, led by leaders like **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**, advocated constitutional methods of protest, while the Extremists, led by **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, demanded more radical measures for achieving independence.
 
• The split weakened the Indian National Congress and delayed the united struggle for independence for several years.
 
• The growing ideological differences, particularly over the **Swadeshi Movement** and boycott of British goods, were the primary reasons behind the split.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Moderates vs. Extremists:**

 
 
• Moderates believed in petitioning the British government for reforms and relied on peaceful negotiations.
 
• Extremists advocated direct action, including boycotts, protests, and promoting Swaraj (self-rule).
 
 
 
• **Swadeshi Movement:**
 
 
• Initiated as a response to the **Partition of Bengal** (1905), it promoted the use of Indian-made goods and boycott of British products.
 
• It became a cornerstone of Extremist ideology during the freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Partition of Bengal:**
 
 
• Announced in 1905 by Lord Curzon, it divided Bengal into East Bengal and West Bengal, allegedly for administrative efficiency.
 
• The move was widely opposed as it was perceived to be a strategy to divide Hindus and Muslims.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Surat Split:**
 
 
• The division within the Congress weakened the nationalist movement for some years.
 
• Unity was restored later during the Lucknow Pact of 1916, when Moderates and Extremists reunited to fight British rule.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the public sector's role in the Indian economy during 1947–1991?

options.text: Dominant in core and heavy industries

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dominant in core and heavy industries.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The public sector played a pivotal role in India's economic development between 1947 and 1991, focusing on core and heavy industries.**
 
• **Key industries such as steel, coal, power generation, oil, and infrastructure were nationalized and spearheaded by the government.**
 
• The public sector acted as a driver for industrialization under India's socialist-inspired economic policies.
 
• **The government aimed to reduce dependency on foreign imports and build self-reliance by establishing public sector enterprises in critical areas.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: Only limited to agriculture:** The public sector was not limited to agriculture during this period. While agriculture was central to the economy, the public sector focused heavily on industrialization and infrastructure development. The Green Revolution of the 1960s was significant, but it was not the sole focus of the government.
 
• **Option 3: Minimal presence:** This is incorrect, as the public sector had a substantial presence during 1947–1991. The government controlled major industries, monopolized sectors like telecommunications and railways, and established public enterprises such as Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) and Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL).
 
• **Option 4: Focused only on foreign trade:** While foreign trade was an important policy area, it was not the primary focus of the public sector. India's economic strategy emphasized self-reliance, import substitution, and industrial development rather than relying on foreign trade.
 
• **Socialist Economic Policies:** India adopted a mixed economy approach, combining elements of socialism and capitalism. The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 laid the foundation for government control over key industries and sectors.
 
• **Five-Year Plans:** India's government implemented central planning through Five-Year Plans, with an emphasis on public sector investments in infrastructure, education, and health.
 
• **Economic Reforms:** The period ended with the 1991 economic liberalization, which shifted the focus from a state-led economy to market-driven policies, reducing the public sector's dominance.

questions.question: According to Ibn Battuta, a Moroccan traveller to India during the Delhi Sultanate, the method of postal system in which the royal horses were used to transfer packages, is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uluq**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term **Uluq** refers to the postal system in the Delhi Sultanate era where royal horses were used to transfer messages and packages.
 
• This system was designed for **fast and efficient communication** across the vast territories of the Sultanate.
 
• The Sultanate maintained a well-structured postal system that relied on horsemen and relay stations to ensure timely delivery.
 
• According to Ibn Battuta, a Moroccan traveler, this system played a significant role in the administration and governance of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• The efficient communication network symbolized the **centralized power and administrative control** of the Sultanate rulers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ibn Battuta**

 
 
• He was a Moroccan traveler and scholar who visited India during the reign of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
 
• He recorded detailed accounts of his travels in his book, "Rihla" (The Journey).
 
• His observations provide valuable insights into the administration, culture, and society of medieval India.
 
 
 
• **Postal Systems in History**
 
 
• Historical postal systems often utilized relay stations and animals such as horses or camels to ensure communication across long distances.
 
• Examples include the Persian Empire's "Royal Road" postal system and the Mongol Empire's "Yam" network.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Sultanate Administration**
 
 
• The Sultanate relied on a centralized bureaucracy to manage its vast territories.
 
• Efficient communication networks like Uluq were vital for maintaining control and implementing policies.
 
 
 
• **Mansabdari System**
 
 
• It was a military-cum-administrative system introduced by Akbar in the Mughal Empire, distinct from the postal systems of the Sultanate.
 
• It categorized officers based on their rank (mansab) and responsibilities.
 
 
 
• **Ikat System**
 
 
• Ikat refers to a traditional textile dyeing technique and has no connection to postal systems.

questions.question: How many small states of present-day Odisha were integrated into the Indian Union at the time of Partition?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**26**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A total of **26 small princely states** of Odisha were integrated into the Indian Union during the period following Partition in 1947.
 
• The integration of these states was part of the larger effort led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India.
 
• These princely states included regions such as **Kalahandi, Bolangir, Mayurbhanj, and others**, which were merged into Odisha.
 
• The process was facilitated by the Instrument of Accession signed by rulers of princely states, agreeing to become part of India.
 
• This integration strengthened administrative and political cohesion in Odisha and the rest of India post-independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Princely States in India:** At the time of independence, India had over 560 princely states ruled by local monarchs under British suzerainty.
 
• **Instrument of Accession:** A legal document that allowed princely states to join India or Pakistan after Partition.
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel's Role:** Patel, known as the "Iron Man of India," played a key role in unifying princely states into the Indian Union.
 
• **Odisha's Historical Context:** Odisha was historically a fragmented region with multiple small princely states before its integration into the Union of India.
 
• **Mayurbhanj:** One of the largest princely states of Odisha, known for its significant contribution to the cultural and administrative consolidation of the region.

questions.question: Which programme aims to ensure access to safe and adequate drinking water through tap connections by 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jal Jeevan Mission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) was launched by the Government of India in **August 2019** to ensure safe and adequate drinking water through tap connections to all households in rural India by **2024**.
 
• It is implemented by the **Ministry of Jal Shakti** under the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation.
 
• The mission focuses on a **community-based approach** to water management, emphasizing decentralized planning and execution.
 
• JJM aims to provide **55 litres of potable water per person per day** to every rural household.
 
• The program also promotes water conservation, source sustainability, and greywater management in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Water Scarcity in India:** India faces acute water scarcity due to **unsustainable water management practices**, over-extraction of groundwater, and pollution of water sources.
 
• **Atal Bhujal Yojana:** A separate scheme aimed at **groundwater management** in priority areas of the country to enhance water sustainability.
 
• **Jal Kranti Abhiyan:** Launched in 2015 by the Ministry of Water Resources to create awareness about **water conservation and management**.
 
• **PM-KUSUM:** Focuses on **solar energy** deployment in agriculture to promote sustainable irrigation practices.
 
• **Greywater Management:** Jal Jeevan Mission emphasizes recycling and reusing **greywater** (wastewater from kitchen and bathrooms) for irrigation and other purposes to reduce water wastage.

questions.question: The distribution of population in India is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**uneven, with variations across regions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The population distribution in India is highly uneven, influenced by geographical, climatic, and economic factors.
 
• Regions like the Indo-Gangetic plains have high population density due to fertile land, favorable climate, and better economic opportunities.
 
• Desert areas (e.g., Rajasthan) and hilly regions (e.g., Himalayan states) have lower population density due to harsh living conditions and limited resources.
 
• Urban areas experience higher population density due to industrialization, employment opportunities, and better infrastructure.
 
• Rural regions may have lower density, except in agriculturally prosperous areas where resources support larger communities.

questions.question: Which of the following elements is classified as an actinoid group element?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thorium**__.

__
 
• **Thorium (Th)** is a chemical element with atomic number 90 and is part of the actinoid series, which includes elements 89 to 103.
 
• Actinoids, including thorium, are found in the f-block of the periodic table and are known for their radioactive properties.
 
• Thorium is a naturally occurring, slightly radioactive metal and is primarily used as a nuclear fuel in thorium reactors.
 
• Among the actinoids, thorium is one of the most abundant and has potential applications in advanced nuclear energy systems.
 
• Thorium is distinct from lanthanides like ytterbium, lanthanum, and cerium, which belong to the f-block but are part of the lanthanoid series.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Actinoid Series:**

 
 
• The actinoid series consists of 15 elements ranging from actinium (Ac) to lawrencium (Lr).
 
• These elements are characterized by the filling of the 5f subshell in their electron configurations.
 
• All actinoids are radioactive, with some like thorium and uranium occurring naturally, while others are synthetic.
 
 
 
• **Thorium Applications:**
 
 
• Thorium is used in molten salt reactors and as a fertile material in nuclear energy production.
 
• Its abundance and low waste production make it a promising alternative to uranium in sustainable nuclear energy.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Lanthanoids and Actinoids:**
 
 
• Lanthanoids (elements 57–71) are less radioactive compared to actinoids.
 
• Actinoids have a greater tendency to form complexes and exhibit variable oxidation states.
 
 
 
• **Ytterbium, Lanthanum, and Cerium:**
 
 
• These elements belong to the lanthanoid series, not the actinoid series.
 
• Lanthanoids are known for their magnetic and luminescent properties and are widely used in electronic devices and catalysts.

questions.question: What legal document allowed Princely States to join either India or Pakistan after independence?

• The **Instrument of Accession** was a legal document introduced by the British Government to allow princely states to join either India or Pakistan after independence in 1947.
 
• Under the provisions of the **Indian Independence Act of 1947**, princely states were given the choice to accede to either of the two dominions or remain independent.
 
• The Instrument of Accession granted the dominion (India or Pakistan) control over specific subjects like defense, foreign affairs, and communications while allowing states to retain autonomy in internal matters.
 
• Notable examples include the accession of Jammu and Kashmir to India on **October 26, 1947**, facilitated by the signing of the Instrument of Accession by Maharaja Hari Singh.
 
• This instrument played a crucial role in shaping the political boundaries of modern-day India and Pakistan.

• It marked the end of British rule in India and resulted in the creation of two dominions—India and Pakistan.
 
• Princely states were given the autonomy to decide their future—join India, Pakistan, or remain independent.
 
 
 
• **Standstill Agreement:**
 
 
• This agreement was signed between the dominions and princely states to maintain the status quo in administrative arrangements until a decision on accession was made.
 
• It provided temporary stability during the transitional phase post-independence.
 
 
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir Accession:**
 
 
• Maharaja Hari Singh of Jammu and Kashmir signed the Instrument of Accession with India during the 1947-1948 conflict.
 
• The decision was influenced by Pakistan-backed tribal invasions in the region.
 
 
 
• **Role of Lord Mountbatten:**

• **Legacy of the Instrument:**

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'intergenerational equity'?

options.text: Fair allocation of resources among various income groups
Fair use of resources to ensure availability for future generations
Fair distribution of resources among present-day nations
Equal economic opportunities for all age-based population groups

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fair use of resources to ensure availability for future generations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Intergenerational equity** refers to the concept of fairness in resource use between current and future generations.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of sustainable development to ensure that **future generations have access to essential resources**.
 
• This principle is widely recognized in international environmental policies, including the **Brundtland Report (1987)**.
 
• It aims to reduce environmental degradation and overexploitation by promoting **long-term resource management.**
 
• Intergenerational equity is a foundational concept in global efforts to combat **climate change, biodiversity loss, and resource depletion.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sustainable Development:** A development approach that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.
 
• **Brundtland Report:** Published by the United Nations in 1987, it introduced the concept of sustainable development and intergenerational equity.
 
• **Climate Change:** A critical area where intergenerational equity is applied, as current emissions impact future generations.
 
• **Biodiversity Conservation:** Protecting ecosystems ensures that future generations inherit a biologically rich and diverse planet.
 
• **Global Frameworks:** Policies like the Paris Agreement and the UN Sustainable Development Goals incorporate intergenerational equity principles.

questions.question: The indigenous CAR‑T therapy has shown maximum efficacy against B‑ALL and which other blood cancer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non‑Hodgkin Lymphoma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• CAR-T therapy (Chimeric Antigen Receptor T-cell therapy) is an advanced form of immunotherapy where T-cells are genetically engineered to attack specific cancer cells.
 
• The indigenous CAR-T therapy developed in India has shown maximum efficacy in treating B-cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (B-ALL) and Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (NHL).
 
• Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma is a diverse group of blood cancers that originate in the lymphatic system, often characterized by the uncontrolled growth of lymphocytes.
 
• Clinical trials have demonstrated significant success rates of CAR-T therapy in relapsed or refractory cases of Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma and B-ALL.
 
• The therapy is a critical breakthrough, offering hope to patients who do not respond to conventional treatments like chemotherapy or radiation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (NHL):**

 
 
• NHL includes various subtypes, such as Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) and Follicular Lymphoma.
 
• It is often associated with symptoms like swollen lymph nodes, fever, night sweats, and weight loss.
 
• Risk factors for NHL include weakened immune systems, certain infections (e.g., HIV, Epstein-Barr virus), and exposure to chemicals.
 
 
 
• **CAR-T Therapy Mechanism:**
 
 
• In CAR-T therapy, a patient’s T-cells are harvested, genetically modified to express chimeric antigen receptors, and reinfused into the patient.
 
• The modified T-cells target and destroy cancer cells expressing specific antigens, such as CD19 in B-ALL and NHL.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of CAR-T Therapy:**
 
 
• Highly effective in treating relapsed or refractory hematological malignancies.
 
• Provides a personalized approach to cancer treatment with durable remissions in many cases.
 
 
 
• **Challenges and Limitations:**
 
 
• CAR-T therapy is expensive and requires specialized infrastructure for production and administration.
 
• Potential side effects include cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and neurotoxicity, which require careful management.
 
 
 
• **Indigenous Development in India:**
 
 
• The development of indigenous CAR-T therapy in India is significant for reducing costs and improving accessibility for patients.
 
• It represents a milestone in the country’s efforts to advance cancer treatment and biotechnology.

questions.question: Who is the highest law officer in a state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Advocate General**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Advocate General is the **highest law officer in a state**, as per Article 165 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• He/she is appointed by the **Governor of the State** and must be qualified to be appointed as a judge of a High Court.
 
• The Advocate General provides legal advice to the state government and represents the state in legal proceedings.
 
• He/she has the right to participate in proceedings of the state legislature but cannot vote.
 
• The office of the Advocate General is analogous to the Attorney General of India at the national level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Attorney General of India:**

 
 
• The Attorney General is the highest law officer at the national level, appointed by the President of India.
 
• He/she advises the Union Government and represents it in legal matters.
 
 
 
• **Qualifications for Advocate General:**
 
 
• Must be a citizen of India.
 
• Should have been an advocate for at least 10 years or a judicial officer for at least 10 years.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Advocate General:**
 
 
• Provides legal counsel to the state government on constitutional and legal matters.
 
• Represents the state in cases before the High Court and Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Advocate General and Attorney General:**
 
 
• The Advocate General operates at the state level, while the Attorney General operates at the national level.
 
• Both are responsible for legal advisories but differ in jurisdiction.
